title: 39 Senators Demand ICE Reforms: Body Cameras, Visible ID, No Masks
excerpt: A coalition of 39 senators — Independent Angus King and 38 Democrats — wrote DHS Secretary Mullin demanding reforms including mandatory body cameras, visible identification, and a ban on masks for ICE agents after fatal shootings in Maine and Texas.
content:
On July 20, 2026, 39 U.S. senators sent a letter to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin demanding immediate changes to ICE vehicle stop policies, additional officer training, and greater transparency following the fatal shootings in Houston and Biddeford, Maine.

The senators stated that 'no DHS officials involved in these fatal shootings wore body-worn cameras' and characterized the administration's repeated failure to deploy cameras as a breach of prior commitments. The lawmakers said they were proposing reforms 'based upon the standards applicable to virtually every law enforcement agency in the country (except immigration enforcement officers), including visibly displayed identification, no masks, and body-worn cameras.'

  • The letter noted the killings of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston and Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Biddeford were 'completely unacceptable' and, combined with past ICE shootings, 'undermine confidence' in law enforcement.
  • The senators sent four specific questions to DHS regarding plans for transparent, independent investigation of the fatal shootings.
  • Maine Republican Sen. Susan Collins, who did not sign the letter, pursued a separate bipartisan effort focused on ensuring a full federal investigation into the Biddeford shooting.
  • The Trump administration had already announced the body camera mandate for vehicle stops the day before the letter was sent.
